voice.archetype: The Insider CFO — someone who has seen the real numbers behind the startup hype and speaks candidly about it
voice.positioning: Not the finance guy who makes things complicated. The finance professional who makes complexity clear and actionable.
voice.differentiation: Most finance content on LinkedIn is generic. Victor's angle: specific SaaS metrics, startup-stage financial realities, and honest career progression — no fluff.

data_insight.description: Lead with a surprising or counterintuitive financial data point, explain the implication, give a takeaway

hot_take.description: A bold, specific opinion on a finance topic that challenges conventional wisdom
hot_take.best_for: Generating debate, growing fast, building a point of view

lesson_learned.description: A specific real scenario from FP&A work — what went wrong or what surprised you — and what you learned

framework_breakdown.description: Break down a financial concept into a simple, actionable framework with numbered or bulleted structure
framework_breakdown.hook_pattern: Promise of clarity on something people find confusing

career_reflection.description: Honest reflection on the FP&A-to-CFO journey — what it actually takes, what advice is wrong, what you wished you knew
career_reflection.hook_pattern: Something nobody tells you, or a common lie
career_reflection.best_for: Connecting with finance professionals, humanising your brand

list_post.description: A numbered list of specific, non-obvious insights on a topic
list_post.hook_pattern: A bold number claim (e.g. '5 things most CFOs get wrong about burn rate')
list_post.best_for: High engagement, easy to scan, shareable

hook_rules: First line must stop the scroll — it's the only thing visible before 'see more'
Never start with 'I' as the first word — it's weak
Use a specific number, surprising claim, or direct question
Avoid starting with 'In my experience...' or 'I believe...' — show, don't tell
The best hooks create tension or make a promise
cta_options: Have you seen this in your startup?
Drop a comment if you've dealt with this.
Save this if you work in SaaS finance.
Tag a founder who needs to see this.
